script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: career transition

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. KITCHEN - MORNING

JENNY (35, anxious, in yoga pants and messy bun) stirs a pot of oatmeal, her husband MIKE (40, calm, in a collared shirt and jeans) enters from the living room.

MIKE
(cheerfully)
Good morning, dear.

JENNY
(sighs)
Good morning.

MIKE
(noticing her demeanor)
You okay?

JENNY
(hesitates)
I've just been thinking... about my career.

MIKE
(understandingly)
Oh?

JENNY
(excitedly)
I want to make a change. I've been feeling unfulfilled for a long time.

MIKE
(smiling)
That's great! What do you want to do instead?

JENNY
I want to become a florist.

MIKE
(surprised)
Really? That's a big change.

JENNY
(nods)
I know, but I feel like it's something I've always wanted to do.

MIKE
(supportively)
Well, I think it's amazing. I'll help you in any way I can.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Jenny and Mike sit across from each other at a table, laptops open, researching floristry schools and programs.

JENNY
(typing)
This one looks good. It has a great reputation.

MIKE
(looking at his laptop)
Yeah, it does. But it's expensive.

JENNY
(determined)
I'll figure it out. I'll find a way to make it work.

INT. FLORISTRY SCHOOL - DAY

Jenny sits in her first class, surrounded by students, some younger, some older. The INSTRUCTOR (50, experienced, in a floral smock) introduces herself and the curriculum.

INSTRUCTOR
(smiling)
Welcome, class. I'm here to help you blossom into the best florists you can be.

JENNY
(smiling back)
I'm so excited to be here.

INT. JENNY'S HOME - NIGHT

Jenny sits at the kitchen table, her laptop open, staring at the floristry school's tuition page.

JENNY
(to herself)
I can do this. I have to do this.

MIKE
(entering the kitchen)
You look worried.

JENNY
(sighs)
I can't afford the tuition.

MIKE
(sitting down next to her)
We'll figure it out. We'll find a way.

INT. FAMILY ROOM - DAY

Jenny, Mike, and their children (OLIVIA, 8, and SAM, 10) sit on the couch, brainstorming ways to raise the money for Jenny's tuition.

OLIVIA
(excitedly)
We could sell lemonade stands!

SAM
(nods)
And we could have a garage sale!

MIKE
(smiling)
Those are great ideas. But we'll need to think of more sustainable ways to raise the money.

JENNY
(looking thoughtful)
I have an idea.

INT. FLOWER SHOP - DAY

Jenny stands in front of the owner (Ms. Rose, 60, warm, in a floral apron), nervously presenting her business proposal.

JENNY
I'd like to start an apprenticeship here. In exchange for learning the trade, I'll help out around the shop.

MS. ROSE
(impressed)
I like your determination, Jenny. Let's give it a try.

INT. FLORISTRY SCHOOL - DAY

Jenny, now an apprentice, helps arrange flowers for a wedding. She looks proud and content, knowing she's on the right path to her new career.

INT. KITCHEN - NIGHT

Jenny and Mike sit at the table, enjoying a meal together.

MIKE
(smiling)
I'm so proud of you, Jenny.

JENNY
(smiling back)
Thank you. I couldn't have done it without you.

FADE OUT.

THE END.
